cards.title: Why attention?
cards.hook: Instead of squeezing everything through one memory, let every token look up what it needs.
cards.visual:
RoleSearch analogy (online shop)
Query (Q)what you type: the information need
Key (K)product titles: compact descriptions to match
Value (V)the full product info returned
Scorequery-key relevance (0.67, 0.58, 0.83, …)
Weightnormalised relevance → highest-weight value
formula: bottleneck, slow sequential, weak long-range memory
Q = question projection; K = log-token keys for matching; V = separate log-token values
example: [CLS] review query: 'heartwarming' gets 38% of the attention → POSITIVE.
cards.memory: Q asks, K answers 'is it me?', V hands over the goods.
cards.trap: Keys are for MATCHING; values are what gets AGGREGATED. Don't swap them.
explain: Attention works like an online search. Your query is what you are looking for; every item has a key (its title, used for matching) and a value (the full content you get back).
Compare the query with every key to get relevance scores, turn the scores into weights that sum to 1, and return a weighted blend of the values.
In self-attention every token does this over the same sentence, so each word can pull in context from any other word directly, with no long recurrent chain.

cards.title: Scores → softmax → weighted sum
cards.src: Lecture 8, slide 74-77; Key points about Attention
cards.trap: Do not just pick the highest-weight value, and do not add the values unweighted.
explain: Step 1: score = dot product of the query with each key (bigger = more aligned), divided by √d_k to keep the numbers moderate.
Step 2: softmax: exponentiate each score and divide by the total, so weights are positive and sum to 1.
Step 3: output = Σ weight × value, computed component by component.

tex.t: \text{score}_i = \frac{\mathbf q\cdot \mathbf k_i}{\sqrt{d_k}}, \qquad w_i = \frac{e^{\text{score}_i}}{\sum_j e^{\text{score}_j}}, \qquad \mathbf z = \sum_i w_i\, \mathbf v_i

cards.title: Self-attention in matrix form
cards.hook: Do it for every token at once with matrix multiplications.
cards.visual:
StepShape (8 tokens, d = 4, d_k = 3)
X (position-aware)8×4
Q = XW_Q, K, V8×3
S = QKᵀ/√d_k8×8
A = row-softmax(S)8×8, each row sums to 1
Z = AV8×3
formula: MHSA → Add & Norm → FFN → Add & Norm (×N)
example: 'control' query row of A: 0.08 0.07 0.12 0.08 0.09 0.16 0.17 0.22 → most attention on 'knob'.
cards.memory: Rows are queries, columns are keys.
cards.trap: Without positional encoding, self-attention can't tell word order.
explain: Do it for all tokens at once: project the (position-aware) inputs X into Q, K, V with three weight matrices; multiply Q by Kᵀ to get every query-key score; softmax each row; multiply by V.
Positional encodings are added to the embeddings so the model knows word order. Multi-head attention runs several heads in parallel, each learning different relationships, then concatenates them.

tex.t: Q = XW_Q,\; K = XW_K,\; V = XW_V, \qquad \text{Attention}(Q,K,V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V

cheat.title: Attention cheat sheet
traps: Each ROW of A sums to 1.
